claims.text: Near-equiatomic NiTi is a shape-memory alloy.
Near-equiatomic NiTi exhibits a martensitic transformation.
The Ni/Ti ratio can be varied and minor alloying elements can be incorporated as a composition-change intervention.
Deviating slightly from the 1:1 Ni/Ti ratio can shift martensitic transformation temperatures.
Adding minor alloying elements to NiTi can shift its martensitic transformation temperatures.
Shifting the transformation temperatures modifies NiTi deformation behavior across temperature.
The relevant structural mediators are martensite–austenite phase boundaries and associated twin-boundary motions.
Changing NiTi composition shifts the relative stability of martensitic and austenitic phases.
A composition-induced shift in phase stability shifts the transformation temperatures.
Changes in phase-transformation behavior alter pseudoelasticity as temperature varies.
Changes in phase-transformation behavior alter the ease of twin-boundary movement as temperature varies.
At lower temperatures, the compositionally modified NiTi will show enhanced martensitic deformation.
At lower temperatures, the compositionally modified NiTi will show a different yielding response.
At higher temperatures, the compositionally modified NiTi will show improved pseudoelasticity due to austenitic behavior.
At higher temperatures, the compositionally modified NiTi will show improved ductility due to austenitic behavior.
The dominant deformation mechanism changes around the intrinsic martensitic-start and austenitic-finish temperatures.
Processing conditions and the exact compositional adjustment affect the magnitude of transformation-temperature and mechanical-property changes.
